text: A post is stood. An oath is spoken. A standard is raised. The cadre does these things or it has nothing to call itself by.
Three brothers. One sister. We stood the same post for nine cycles. The standard was always raised by the first relief.
When the Fall came, the standard was raised. We did not relieve. We did not abandon. The standard burned with the post.
Reya, the second sister of the post. She polished the standard the morning of the Fall. The polish is in the standard you held in the dream-loom; that is the Reya part of it.
Ordered. The order was correct. The execution was incorrect. The cadre was the execution; the cadre paid. We did not contest the order; we contested the executor.
I will not name him. He has a name in the Hierarchy ledger; the ledger is sealed; I respect the sealing.
Yes. Each cycle. The cadre would. The cadre does, in the dream-loom, on every Foundation Day; the contestation is itself a form of post-standing.
A standard is the post made portable. The cloth is incidental. The cadre is the standard.
A standard is a post made portable. The cadre is the post made personal.
If you ask why we have these things — you have not stood a watch.
Stand the watch. I will be in the dream-loom with you for the first hour; do not speak to me. Then I will go.
The cadre relieves. The cadre votes the post in the relief words. Disagreement is fine; it is the standard that requires agreement.
Yes. We disagreed about the executor. We did not disagree about the post. The disagreement was honourable; the post was honoured.
A broken cadre still stands the post until the standard is taken down with the relief words. The breaking is a slow thing; the post is a fast thing.
Pageantry is what the audience sees. Ceremony is what the post requires. The audience is, mostly, irrelevant to the cadre.
The standard burned. The standard outlasted. Both are true.
What burned was the cloth. What outlasted is, you, holding it.
She polished it the morning of. She did not say. Polishing is a kind of knowing without naming; she was a polisher; she knew.
No. We could have refused the executor. The order was correct; the executor was wrong; we did not refuse correctly. We refused after, in dream-loom; the refusing is what bleeds through.
It is the cadre's contestation. We argue with the executor in posthumous voice. The argument is the afterlife; the afterlife is mostly an argument.
When the standard is reraised in a hand we trust. We have not seen that hand yet. We are watching.
Most cadres did not have a Necromancer. Mine does. Forgetting is a verb; she has named the subject. The cadre has not been forgotten on her watch.
The standard is yours to reraise. I will not choose where. I will name only the requirement: it must outlast the act.
Reraise it for the next bearer. Or reraise it for the cadre. Or bury it. The cadre will accept any of the three.
Accepted. The standard goes to him. The relief words are in the dream-loom; he will hear them at the next post.
Accepted. The standard becomes the cadre's, not a bearer's. The post becomes a roll; the roll keeps. This is harder. The harder thing is, on most days, the right thing.
Each cycle. Until a hand we trust takes it from the roll. Then the roll closes; the standard returns to the bearer.
Then the roll is the cadre's afterlife in cloth form. Worse fates exist. We will watch.

Honest. The cadre accepts. The dream-loom thread closes. We will not bleed through again. The cloth goes under the post-stone at Mechronis. You did not come here for a fight; you came here for an answer; you have it.
A standard has been raised. The cadre stands at attention through the dream-loom. The relief words are spoken in your hand tonight.
A post is empty. Three brothers and a sister stand it with me tonight. The standard does not lower; the post is held.
The cadre voted relief. The relief words are correct. The post passes to the next bearer. Stand it well.
Spell them as I gave them. Reya's name has the soft consonant in the middle; the Authority misspelled it twice.
Jericho. The relief words are mine to give. They are yours to hear.
Sentinel. Your post is correctly stood.
Zealot. Your cause is being argued in the Refuge.
